# Dave Moore

Dave is the second husband of [[wiki/people/diane-moore|Diane]], Dan's
maternal grandmother, and therefore Dan's step-grandfather by marriage. He is
never quoted, never messages anyone in the corpus, and appears in exactly nine
records across five years — but he is on the wrong side of every one of them,
and the operator's 2026 identification of the "grandparents who already hated
you" as **"Dian and Dave"** makes him half of the pair whose hostility shaped
the most consequential eight hours of the Fran sequence.

He matters for one specific reason: he is the only person in the family
architecture who exercised authority over Fran's death without holding any
relationship to her. Diane was her daughter. Dave was her daughter's husband,
and in the final week he was the one the hospital was talking to.

## What the record has him doing

**Speaking for her when she could not be reached.** On 2018-04-01, three days
before Fran died, Dan reported the arrangement twice within eighteen minutes,
and the second time with the detail that makes it strange:

> "meanwhile diane moore hasn't been able to be reached by anyone. dave is
> 'speaking on her behalf' and it's very unusual stuff"
>
> "no comment required. it's just wild, the social workers are talking to dave
> moore about the day-to-day stuff lol"

The quotation marks around *speaking on her behalf* are Dan's. The situation
he is describing is a hospital discussing a dying woman's daily care with a
man who is not her relative, because her only child was unreachable — while
the two people who had kept her out of a nursing home for three years had been
formally excluded from the rotation.

**Writing the letter, on Dan's reading.** Two days later, holding the document
that demanded the keys to 155 Virginia and closed with a trespassing clause,
Dan's first conclusion was about authorship:

> "i think dave wrote it — read the last paragraph. 'any violation of the
> rules will be considered trespassing' ....so if i violated the rules by not
> leaving the key i would be trespassing?"

This is a read of prose style by its recipient, not evidence of authorship,
and the page holds it as such. But it is consistent with the social-worker
arrangement two days earlier — the same substitution, the instrument issued in
Diane's name and produced in Dave's voice.

**Everything else is a pair.** He appears in the corpus almost exclusively as
the second half of "Diane and Dave," and the pairing itself is the finding —
Dan does not treat them as a person and her husband but as a single actor:

| Date | Record |
|---|---|
| 2016-08-13 | *"Diane and Dave went ALL out this year on a very creative and not the same thing they got last year birthday gift for gram"* — sarcasm, and the only record of either of them marking Fran's birthday |
| 2018-04-01 | *"i don't know if anyone wants a 45 minute roasting of diane and dave"* — Dan on whether to speak at the service |
| 2018-04-03 | *"just glad that diane and dave aren't super upset, they're probably busy working through the tragedy of her death and that's why they haven't checked in on her"* — written the day before Fran died |
| 2018-08-01 | Annie, four months after the funeral: *"Wait wtf. Your mom ran into Dian and Dave today?!"* |
| 2020-03-28 | *"i hope diane and dave both drown in their own vomit after simultaneously contracting coronavirus"* |

The 2018-08-01 line is the only documented post-funeral contact between the
two halves of the family, and Annie's reaction to it — *wait wtf* — is the
measure of how unexpected it was.

## Why he gets a page

The wiki's rule is one page per entity and no entity too small to have one,
and Dave clears the bar on evidence alone. But he earns it on a second ground:
he is the cleanest instance in the family material of
[[wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism]]. The template that page
describes is authority exercised at a distance, through paperwork and proxies,
by people who are not present and do not do the work. Diane at least had
standing — she was the heir and the daughter. Dave had none, and he is the one
who talked to the social workers and, probably, wrote the letter.

He is also the reason the operator's two-word answer changed the shape of the
Fran material rather than just correcting a name. The earlier reading had Dan
fearing a generic pair of grandparents — Diane and George — during the
keno-morning fall, an eight-hour delay in treating a fallen 97-year-old
explained by inheritance anxiety. The couple he actually feared is the couple
that then served the notice, wrote the letter, took the hospital's calls and
sold the Florida condo. The fear was not a mood. It was a forecast, and it was
right.

## Gaps

- **Everything biographical.** No age, no occupation, no location, no surname
  confirmation beyond the two 2018 messages that give it. Whether he and Diane
  are still married, or still living, is unknown.
- **Whether he actually wrote the letter.** Dan's read is the only evidence.
  The document itself is not in `raw/`.
- **Whether he had any relationship with Fran at all** before the final weeks.
  The one record of him marking her birthday is a joke at his expense.
- **What he is to Suz.** He is her stepfather by her mother's second marriage,
  and the corpus never records a single word between them.
